title: Net investment income tax: 3.8 percent on rents and gains above a threshold
rule: An individual owes 3.8 percent tax on the lesser of net investment income or modified adjusted gross income above $250,000 (joint return or surviving spouse), $125,000 (married filing separately) or $200,000 (otherwise); the thresholds are not indexed. Net investment income includes rents and net gain from selling property, less allocable deductions, unless earned in the ordinary course of a nonpassive trade or business. A regulatory safe harbor deems a real estate professional's rents and gains from a rental real estate activity in which they participate over 500 hours in the year, or in five of the ten prior years, to arise in a trade or business.
changeWatch: Any amendment to section 1411 (the dollar thresholds are not indexed, so they change only by statute) or to the regulations at 26 CFR 1.1411-4; estates and trusts use a different threshold, the amount at which the top bracket in section 1(e) begins.
